A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The player's downward check tests bits 0–1 at $0C57 and, for the next column, at $0C7A; the player's horizontal checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile. For entities, the downward scan at $450C tests bits 0–1 at $4532 and $4542, and the horizontal test at $460C reads four attributes through $4632 (at $464C), keeping bit 1 of the first two and bit 0 of the last two.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell. A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code to one 40-character screen row below the first cell. For a nonnegative byte, subtract 5 with carry set; if it borrows, continue, otherwise call $43A2 with the result, except that a result of 5 or more stores 9 and passes 4. Continue at $A30C. Load Y from $1AE4,X and read the byte at $A32E,Y. If negative, take its eight-bit two’s complement and call $4342 to move up by it; otherwise call $4368 with the byte unchanged to move down. Call $792C and $732A. If $732A returns carry set and $1A6D,X is zero or negative, branch to $A65F. Otherwise call $7227; branch to $A64A on carry set or return on carry clear.

Ten frame offsets, $00, $02, $04, $06, $06, $04, $04, $04, $02, $00, one for each step of state 2. State 1 reads $1AE4,X. If nonnegative, decrement the field and call $43F0, which moves the object right, with its original value when $A7FE is nonnegative, or $43A2, which moves it left, when it is negative. Then call $44DE, which moves the object down by A=$1AF5,X with a collision check. If carry is clear, increment $1AF5,X and return. If carry is set, continue at $A7A0, which selects state 2. Clear $1AC2,X and set $1A07,X to 1. Load $19E5,X, add 2 with carry clear if $A7FE is nonnegative, then clear carry and add another 2. Store the result in $19E5,X and $19C3,X, set $1AB1,X to 2 and return. This arithmetic is binary when decimal mode is clear.

State 2 reads $1AC2,X. If it is less than 2, increment that field, double its original value, clear carry, add $19E5,X and store the low byte at $19C3,X, then return. Otherwise continue at $A7D7. This addition is binary when decimal mode is clear.
